Dimitri drives Rose off campus to be tested by Arthur Schoenberg, a legendary retired guardian, and they find him dead in the house he was guarding, along with the entire Moroi family in his care. The scene is wrong in ways that frighten the guardians who examine it: Strigoi worked together in a coordinated group, which their nature is supposed to prevent, and they had living humans helping them get past a home's defenses. Similar attacks are reported elsewhere, and it becomes clear that someone is organizing them. The Academy tightens its security and cancels the students' usual travel plans, and the adults begin arguing about what the change means for a society that has always relied on isolated, defensive guarding.

Rose's mother Janine, a famous guardian Rose has barely lived with, arrives at the school in connection with the attacks, and their reunion is cold on both sides. Rose is stung publicly when her mother dismisses her ambitions in front of other novices. Christian's aunt Tasha Ozera also visits, scarred and outspoken, and argues to anyone who will listen that Moroi should be trained to fight with their magic rather than depending entirely on dhampirs; the idea splits students and staff alike. With winter break approaching and travel considered unsafe, the school relocates the holiday to a Moroi-owned ski resort in Idaho under heavy guardian protection. Mason, who has made no secret of wanting to be more than Rose's friend, is glad of the chance to spend the break near her.

At the resort Rose meets Adrian Ivashkov, a wealthy, idle royal Moroi who drinks constantly, sees the auras around people, and turns out to be a spirit user like Lissa. Mia Rinaldi, who tormented Rose and Lissa the previous year, is also there, quiet and shut out by the royals she once courted. Rose keeps Mason at arm's length while spending as much time as she can near Dimitri, and then learns what Tasha has actually come to propose: she wants Dimitri as her guardian, and she wants a life and children with him. Dimitri does not refuse outright. Rose, who cannot offer him anything of the kind without both of them losing everything, has to watch him consider it.

Queen Tatiana arrives with her court and singles Rose out at a public dinner, warning her away from Adrian in front of the room; Rose answers back and is humiliated for it. Janine gives Rose a small blue eye charm sent by the father Rose has never been told anything about. Mia learns that her mother has been killed in one of the Strigoi attacks, and the news changes her: she stops competing for status and starts asking guardians to teach her to fight, having already taught herself to use water magic offensively. The argument over whether Moroi should learn to defend themselves grows louder throughout the resort. Rose, meanwhile, overhears guardians discussing a group of Strigoi believed to be nesting in the city of Spokane, and repeats it to Mason.

Mason, hungry to prove himself and to impress Rose, leaves the resort for Spokane to hunt the Strigoi, taking Eddie and Mia with him. Rose realizes what he has done and follows with Christian, intending to drag them back before anyone is hurt. The five of them are found first. The Strigoi in Spokane have human servants who can move by day, and the group is taken while the sun is up and locked in the basement of a house. Their captors are Isaiah, an ancient Strigoi who enjoys drawing the situation out, and Elena, who is only interested in the practicalities. The captives are kept as a food supply, fed on one at a time, and no one outside knows where they are.

In the basement the group works out a plan that depends on Christian's fire magic and on getting a silver stake into someone's hands. When the moment comes, Christian burns Elena and Rose engages Isaiah. Mason, who had gotten out and come back for them, throws himself at Isaiah to keep him off Rose, and the Strigoi kills him with a single movement. Rose, beyond thought, destroys both Strigoi. Guardians reach the house shortly afterwards and bring the survivors out. Rose is not blamed by anyone in authority, and is marked with two molnija tattoos for the Strigoi she killed, but she knows she gave Mason the location and then failed to stop him. In the days that follow she begins to see him standing silently nearby, saying nothing, and cannot decide whether she is being haunted or losing her mind to the darkness she carries for Lissa.

Back at the Academy, Rose refuses counselling and holds her grief in. Dimitri turns down Tasha's offer and stays at St. Vladimir's, and he and Rose finally say aloud what they have both been avoiding. They also agree on why it cannot happen: in a real attack each would save the other before saving Lissa, which would make them useless as her guardians. Mia leaves the resort a friend rather than an enemy, having chosen to learn to fight, and the debate Tasha started is now being had across Moroi society. Rose returns to training with a new, colder motivation, still seeing Mason at the edge of her vision and telling nobody.

characters.description: Living on Preservation Station under Dr. Mensah's protection, the SecUnit has legal status of a sort, a security consultant's job, and no friends at all in Station Security, which regards an armed construct wandering its corridors as a problem it did not ask for. It has agreed not to hack station systems, a restriction it resents continuously and which makes ordinary investigative work far harder than it should be.
characters.name: Murderbot

characters.description: The head of Station Security, professional, unimpressed, and openly opposed to a construct taking part in her investigation. She cooperates because Dr. Mensah asks her to, and sets conditions the SecUnit has to work inside rather than around.
characters.name: Senior Officer Indah

characters.description: The planetary administrator who holds the SecUnit's contract as a legal shield and is the reason it lives on Preservation at all. She backs its involvement in the investigation and absorbs the political consequences of doing so.
characters.name: Dr. Ayda Mensah

characters.description: A Station Security officer assigned to the case, and one of the few willing to work alongside the SecUnit without making an issue of what it is.
characters.name: Officer Aylen

characters.description: A friend from the old survey team, cheerfully willing to be pulled into an investigation and genuinely useful for the parts of it that require talking to people, which the SecUnit would rather avoid.
characters.name: Dr. Ratthi

characters.description: The lawyer from the old survey team, who handles the legal side of a construct doing police work in a polity that has never had to think about either.
characters.name: Pin-Lee

characters.description: The augmented human from the old survey team, quick inside the feed and useful for exactly the data work the SecUnit has promised not to do by hacking.
characters.name: Dr. Gurathin

recaps.ending: The murder is solved: the victim was working for an operation smuggling people out of corporate indenture and into Preservation, and was killed by the people he was working with once he became a danger to them. The SecUnit finds where the trafficked humans are being held and gets them out before they can be disposed of to close off the investigation, and those responsible are taken into custody by Station Security. The rescued people are taken in by Preservation, which treats granting asylum to anyone fleeing being owned as an ordinary obligation rather than a favour. Professionally, the case changes the SecUnit's position on the station: Senior Officer Indah, who fought its involvement from the first day, concedes that the work was done properly, cooperation between it and Station Security becomes possible, and the restrictions on its access to station systems are eased. Nothing about its legal status is settled - it is still a construct living in a polity with no category for it - but it now has a working relationship with the people who police the place it lives, and a demonstrated reason to be there beyond Dr. Mensah's protection. It remains unwilling to admit that it found any of it interesting.
recaps.in_short: A murdered human turns up on Preservation Station, which has neither the crime rate nor the expertise to deal with one. Dr. Mensah puts the SecUnit on the investigation over the objections of Station Security, whose head, Senior Officer Indah, permits it only on condition that the SecUnit works with her officers and stops hacking station systems. Reduced to drones, physical evidence and talking to people, it establishes that the victim reached the station illegally and was moved after death. The trail leads to an operation smuggling humans escaping corporate indenture into Preservation and holding them hidden for leverage. The victim was part of that operation and was killed by his own associates to keep it from being exposed. The SecUnit locates the concealed refugees, gets them out before they can be killed to bury the case, and hands the traffickers to Station Security. The rescued people are granted asylum, Indah's opinion of the SecUnit improves enough to matter, and it gets some of its access back without conceding that it likes anybody.

recaps.text: Previously: the SecUnit hacked its own governor module, protected a Preservation survey team from the company GrayCris, and then traveled alone until GrayCris took Dr. Mensah hostage, at which point it came back and got her out, nearly destroying itself in the process. It now lives on Preservation Station. Mensah legally holds its contract purely as a shield; in practice it is free, employed as her security consultant, and the subject of continuing argument in a polity where nobody is property and nobody knows what to do with an armed construct that has opinions. It has agreed not to hack station systems, which it finds close to intolerable. Station Security in particular does not want it there. Chronologically this story falls before Network Effect: nothing beyond the rescue of Dr. Mensah has happened yet.

A dead human is found on Preservation Station, deliberately killed - something the station is not equipped to investigate, having almost no violent crime and no experience of it. The body carries no identity records, has no obvious reason to be where it was found, and shows signs of having been moved after death. Dr. Mensah puts the SecUnit onto the case over the objections of Station Security, whose head, Senior Officer Indah, agrees only under conditions: the SecUnit works with her officers rather than around them, and does not touch station systems without permission. Deprived of the hacking that would normally have answered most of this in minutes, it has to work with drones, physical evidence, camera coverage it is allowed to request, and conversations with humans, all of which it hates. The immediate question is simple and unanswerable: who was the victim, and how did an unidentified person get onto a station that logs everyone who arrives?

Working the case with the security officers, the SecUnit establishes that the victim never went through any legitimate entry process and had been on the station for some time, hidden. It reconstructs where the body was moved from and how, which narrows the search to the parts of the station used for cargo and transit rather than for living. The first theory is that a corporate agent - a bond company or a rival of Preservation's - has put someone aboard, and the SecUnit is conscious throughout that it is the obvious suspect for any violence on the station and cannot afford to be wrong about anything. The evidence points elsewhere: to something being moved quietly through the station, with the victim as part of the arrangement rather than its target.

The investigation uncovers the business behind the killing: people are being trafficked. A group of humans escaping indenture in the corporate systems has been brought to Preservation illegally, and the operation moving them is not charitable - the refugees are being held hidden and used as leverage by the people running the route. The victim was part of that operation. The SecUnit and the officers work backwards along the chain of hiding places, forged transit records and cargo movements toward wherever the group is being kept, knowing that the moment the traffickers realize an investigation is closing on them, the hidden people stop being an asset and become a liability.

The SecUnit finds where the refugees are being held and gets them out, dealing with the traffickers' people and a hostile confrontation in the station's cargo levels before anyone can be killed to cover the operation. The murder is explained: the victim was killed by the people he was working with, to stop him exposing what they were doing. Those responsible are taken into custody by Station Security. The rescued refugees, whose whole situation exists because they were running from being owned, are granted asylum on Preservation, which is precisely the sort of thing the polity exists to do. Senior Officer Indah, who spent the case objecting to the SecUnit's presence, ends it acknowledging that the work was good, and the terms of the SecUnit's access to station systems are loosened as a result. The SecUnit remains unwilling to admit that it enjoyed any part of it.
